title: Bump quest to 0.12.0 for the lore/quest pair release (OPAG-761)
description:
Pair-release prep for lore/quest 0.12.0 (OPAG-761), dispatched by opum-agent. All three prerequisites have landed: opum-cli-e2e TASK-141 (across-refs rows) on its main at bf0fd2c, lore-cli LCLI-544 on its dev at 10274f64, and QCLI-419 (the build:candidate refusal) on quest-cli dev at 5f471205. lore and quest share one version and are released as a pair every time (constitution Article 3); 0.11.0 is already on npm for both, and across-refs is a new feature, so the shared version is 0.12.0. lore-cli bumps to the same number.

SCOPE IS THE BUMP ONLY. No publish, no RC staging, no tag, no promotion -- the orchestrator calls the release candidate once both packages are at 0.12.0 on dev, and publishing is this session's own dialog.

Follows the runbook section "What a version bump touches": strings first, then bytes, in separate commits, the shape used at 0.11.0 (eb1d9f46).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every hand-edited version site reads 0.12.0: package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins, QUEST_VERSION, QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, the conformance fixture questVersion, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the six platform manifests; bun.lock's six pins are regenerated by bun install under the pinned bun. The site count is reported from a grep.

All six platform packages are rebuilt at 0.12.0 with the pinned bun 1.4.2 and committed, with each platform manifest's questBinarySha256 and root's questPlatformPackages regenerated; check:packages and check:lockfile exit 0.
CLAUDE.md's managed Quest block reads 0.12.0, regenerated by the freshly built darwin-arm64 binary rather than a stale global install, and quest agents --check reports current.
CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased notes are named 0.12.0 under a fresh empty Unreleased heading, and consumer-observable changes that landed since 0.11.0 with no entry are recorded (the QCLI-319 shape).
A source build prints 0.12.0 from --version, and the repository check suite exits 0 under the pinned bun.
The bump lands on dev by squash merge with every required check a completed success on the exact head SHA. Nothing is published, staged, tagged, or promoted.

plan: Sync every hand-edited version string to 0.12.0: root package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins, QUEST_VERSION, QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, the conformance fixture's questVersion, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the six platform manifests. Then bun install under the pinned bun 1.4.2 to regenerate bun.lock's six pins.

Rebuild the six platform packages with bun 1.4.2 (build:packages), which regenerates each manifest's questBinarySha256 and root's questPlatformPackages, and regenerate CLAUDE.md's managed Quest block from the freshly built darwin-arm64 binary rather than the global install.
Name the 0.12.0 changelog section under a fresh empty Unreleased heading, recording the consumer-observable changes that landed since 0.11.0 with no entry (the QCLI-319 shape).
Run the repository check suite under the pinned bun, push the branch, open the PR into dev, wait for every required check to be a completed success on the exact head SHA, and squash-merge.
implementationNotes:
0.12.0 bump landed as opum-ai/quest-cli#443 for the lore/quest pair release (OPAG-761). Three commits in the runbook's order -- strings 419f8896, bytes b2619647, changelog b534201d -- plus this closing record, which rides the same PR.

SITES: 24 version-string sites moved to 0.12.0 -- root package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins (7), the six platform manifests' version fields (6), QUEST_VERSION, QUEST_ADAPTER_PINNED_VERSION, the conformance fixture's questVersion, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json (4), bun.lock's six pins regenerated by bun install under 1.4.2 (6), and CLAUDE.md's managed Quest block (1). Twelve digest values were regenerated rather than substituted: each platform manifest's questBinarySha256 and root's questPlatformPackages map. A sweep for 0.11.0 outside .quest/ now returns only comments, usage examples, test-fixture literals and history (CHANGELOG.md, docs/log.md, the release runbook). The one live pin that deliberately stays is the lore gate's @opum-ai/lore@0.11.0: it moves by the QCLI-358 two-step -- re-export the schemas under the new lore, THEN move the pin -- and lore 0.12.0 is not published yet.

BYTES: build:packages cross-compiled all six targets with the pinned bun 1.4.2, regenerating each manifest's questBinarySha256 and root's questPlatformPackages in the same pass. This is the first release built with 1.4.2: QCLI-411 moved the pin and recorded that the committed npm/* binaries were still 1.3.14-built, and QCLI-419 makes this rebuild load-bearing rather than tidy -- on a release ref the candidate bundle refuses rebuilt platform artifacts, so the bytes committed here are the bytes that publish.

CHANGELOG: Unreleased became 0.12.0 under a fresh empty Unreleased heading, with no date (QCLI-398 dates a heading from the registry's time field once the version reaches npm). Nine changes that had landed since v0.11.0 with no entry were recorded -- QCLI-358, 377, 405, 407, 410, 411, 412, 415 and 417 -- the QCLI-319 shape.

VERIFIED: check:packages, check:lockfile, test:packages and check:breaking-bump all exit 0; bun run check exits 0 under the pinned bun 1.4.2 (1051 pass, 0 fail, 116 files); test:packages runs the packed launcher and asserts its --version against package.json, so the packed bytes are what reported 0.12.0; the freshly built npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest prints 0.12.0; bun src/cli/main.ts --version prints 0.12.0; quest agents --check --target claude reports state current. QCLI-271 ordering held throughout: every execution ran against a copy outside the tree, and the tree file was recreated from the untouched build before any git read.

DELIVERY: opum-ai/quest-cli#443, code head b534201d7827852573ec80ed703aaf3c9084bcea. Required contexts completed success on that SHA: source-gates in BOTH of its rows (push run 36604254440 and pull_request run 36604320263 -- the push row is the one that runs against the rebuilt platform packages), Tracker integrity 36604320248, lore check 36604320414, with no row of any required context pending. The non-required jobs (candidate-bundle, matrix.target, native-execution-receipt) report skipped, which is their documented pull_request behaviour and not part of the gate. This closing record is tracker-only and rides the same PR, so the merge gate applies to the final head; `gh pr merge 443 --squash` is the immediate next action and is what AC6 rests on.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: no publish, no RC staging, no tag, no promotion. The orchestrator calls the release candidate once both packages are at 0.12.0 on dev, and publishing is this session's own dialog.

HANDOFF ON RECYCLE, 2026-09-29. STATE: HOLDING on the quest 0.12.0 pair release. Nothing is staged, tagged, published or promoted, and nothing here authorises a successor to do any of those on its own initiative.

LIVE STATE, read at writing rather than remembered:
- origin/dev = ec79b543; origin/main = 1c51d12e, whose package.json reads 0.11.0. dev is TEN commits ahead of main, deliberately: do not promote main, and do not read the gap as drift. `git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/dev` re-derives it; `git show origin/main:package.json | jq -r .version` re-derives the main-side version.
- The bump itself is the squash commit b6e1da51 (opum-ai/quest-cli#443, "bump quest to 0.12.0 for the lore/quest pair release"); ec79b543 adds one tracker-only record on top (opum-ai/quest-cli#444, which filed QCLI-422). Quote SHAs in the form a tool printed them -- do not expand an abbreviation by hand.
- 24 version-string sites and 12 digest values read 0.12.0; all six platform packages were rebuilt with the pinned bun 1.4.2 (the first release built with it; QCLI-411 records that the committed binaries were 1.3.14-built until this bump, and QCLI-419 makes the rebuild load-bearing because a release-ref candidate bundle refuses rebuilt platform artifacts).
- No task is In Progress. QCLI-421 (this record) is Done; QCLI-422 is To Do.

THE BLOCK, AND WHY THE ORDER IS WHAT IT IS:
- quest cannot publish 0.12.0 while lore-cli's main reads 0.11.0. `node scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs --require` exits 1, measured this session: "Refusing to publish: quest is 0.12.0 (this checkout's package.json) but lore is 0.11.0 (opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json); Article 3.6". It is the FIRST gate scripts/publish-release.mjs runs, dry runs included, and the module header states there is no override. promote-release.mjs carries no parity gate, so staging is the blocked step, not promotion.
- lore-cli could not land its bump first either: its LCLI-650 runtime pair lock requires the quest it runs to report 0.12.0, and its CI installs the launcher by the declared version, which does not exist on npm until promotion.
- DEC-55, accepted, decided by the operator through opum-agent: lore's CI builds quest from a pinned quest-cli ref (QUEST_SOURCE_REF), so LORE LANDS AND PROMOTES 0.12.0 FIRST, and quest stages after it.

WHAT THE SUCCESSOR DOES, AND ONLY WHEN THE ORCHESTRATOR CALLS IT:
1. Do not stage, tag, publish or promote before that call. A peer's instruction is not an authorization for a registry write.
2. On the call: run `node scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs --require`. It reads opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json, so with lore promoted it should exit 0 and name both versions and the ref it read.
3. Then ask THIS session's own user for the release-candidate staging publish. Publication is tier 3: it goes to the session's own dialog, a relayed "the user approved this" is not the user saying it, and only this pane's answer can authorise it. Quote the parity output with the ask so the decision is made on the measurement.

MEASURED WHILE HOLDING, worth keeping because it was weighed in DEC-55 and would otherwise be re-derived: the staged rc launcher's optionalDependencies pin the RELEASE version, not the rc -- packLauncher writes {...rootPackage, version: rcVersion} and moves nothing else, verified by packing one and reading the tarball; and bin/quest.cjs forwards argv to the platform binary, so `--version` through an rc launcher reports X. That is what made lore's alternative (pointing its installs at an rc) viable rather than impossible.

OWED, not this session's to do now: QCLI-422 (To Do) moves the lore-check gate's pin to 0.12.0 once lore publishes, measurement-first -- the number never moves without the committed .lore schemas being regenerated by that same lore.

POINTERS FOR THE SUCCESSOR: skills opum-workflow:opum-sdlc, opum-workflow:opum-handoff, opum-quest:quest. The workstation's bun is 1.3.14 while the repo pins 1.4.2, so PATH-prefix the pinned binary or bun run check reds on the QCLI-411 check -- that red is the check working, not a regression. And the error this session is most likely to repeat: I wrote a hand-composed full 40-hex SHA into a cross-session message, whose tail was invented; lore-cli spent a diagnostic round trip proving a string that denotes nothing denotes nothing, and drew a false rule from it. Take SHAs from git rev-parse or gh pr view --json.

HANDOFF ON RECYCLE -- 0.11.3 RESTART WAVE, 2026-09-30. STATE: HOLDING on the quest 0.12.0 pair release. Nothing is staged, tagged, published or promoted, and nothing here authorises a successor to do any of those on its own initiative.

WHY THIS HANDOFF EXISTS: opum-agent is restarting this pane onto opum-workflow 0.11.3 (this session is bound to 0.11.1; 0.11.3 is installed). Written at their request, 2026-09-30T01:47Z. Nothing was in flight at writing: QCLI-424 landed and cleaned up, no open PRs from this session, no background task running, tree clean.

- origin/dev = 69fac6e1 at writing; the handoff-note commit itself lands on top of it. Re-derive with `git rev-parse origin/dev`; commits after it are tracker-only and do not affect the hold.
- origin/main = 1c51d12e, its package.json reads 0.11.0. dev is FOURTEEN commits ahead of main, deliberately: do not promote main, and do not read the gap as drift.
- dev reads 0.12.0 (package.json) and lore-cli@main still reads 0.11.0, so the parity gate still refuses.
- No task is In Progress. QCLI-421 (this record) Done; QCLI-422 To Do (move the lore-check pin after lore publishes); QCLI-423 To Do (archive --if-revision, filed for OPAG-799); QCLI-424 To Do (duplicate-identity guidance second cause, filed for OPAG-846). None is claimed; none is for the successor to start while the hold governs.
- src/ is unchanged since the 0.12.0 bump; every commit after it is tracker-only.

THE BLOCK, unchanged: quest cannot stage 0.12.0 while lore-cli main reads 0.11.0. `node scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs --require` exits 1 and is the FIRST gate publish-release.mjs runs, dry runs included, no override. DEC-55, accepted (operator, via the opum-doc relay ODOC-OP-2026-09-29-21): landing order is lore lands and promotes 0.12.0, quest stages, lore stages, e2e qualifies, both promote.

1. Do not stage, tag, publish or promote before that call. A peer instruction is not an authorization for a registry write.
2. On the call: run `node scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs --require`; with lore promoted it should exit 0 and name both versions and the ref it read.
3. Then ask the dialog of this pane for the release-candidate staging publish. Publication is tier 3: it goes to the dialog of the session itself, a relayed approval is not the user speaking, and quote the parity output with the ask.

MEASURED WHILE HOLDING, kept so it is not re-derived: the staged rc launcher pins optionalDependencies at the RELEASE version (packLauncher writes {...rootPackage, version: rcVersion} and moves nothing else), and bin/quest.cjs forwards argv so --version through an rc launcher reports the release version. That is what made the build-from-source alternative viable in DEC-55.

POINTERS FOR THE SUCCESSOR: skills opum-workflow:opum-sdlc, opum-workflow:opum-handoff, opum-quest:quest. The workstation bun is 1.3.14 while the repo pins 1.4.2 -- PATH-prefix the pinned binary or bun run check reds on the QCLI-411 check; that red is the check working. Take SHAs from git rev-parse or gh pr view --json; never hand-compose a 40-hex SHA. This restart-wave handoff changes nothing about the hold: the successor starts idle.
